questions.question: What is a fuel? Name one solid, one liquid and one gas fuel.
questions.expected_answer: A fuel is a material that has energy stored in it, which is usually released by burning. Solid: coal, wood, charcoal or candle wax. Liquid: petrol, diesel or paraffin. Gas: LP gas or natural gas.

questions.question: Explain why food is a fuel and how we measure the energy in food.
questions.expected_answer: Food has energy stored in it, which our bodies release slowly to move, grow, keep warm and think. Food energy is measured in kilojoules, shown on food labels.

questions.question: Where did the energy in wood and coal come from? Why are coal and oil non-renewable?
questions.expected_answer: It came from the Sun. Plants captured energy from sunlight and stored it; wood is part of a tree, and coal formed from ancient plants buried for millions of years. Coal and oil are non-renewable because they took millions of years to form and cannot be replaced once used.
